newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen down 75-80 bcf in weekly AGA.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen down 75-80 bcf in weekly AGA.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to fall by 75-80 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said Wednesday.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for a drawdown ranging from 50 to 97 bcf for the week ended Nov 22.
"It was pretty cold last week. I think some people dipped into storage. We should cut the consuming region East surplus," one Midwest trader said.
Last week's decline of 86 bcf was substantially higher than most had expected.
"The weather wasn't as severe as the previous week so the number should be a little lower," a Houston-based trader said, referring to the weather in the eastern two-thirds of the U.S.
Weekly drawdowns in November 1995 averaged 74 bcf.

In the last report, Eastern stocks fell by 58 bcf to 92 percent of capacity, still slightly above year-ago. Producing region inventories slipped 29 bcf to 69 percent full and continued to seriously lag 1995 levels of about 83 percent of capacity.

For the same week last year, total inventories fell by 61 bcf, meaning a draw today in the expected range would widen the gap to 1995 to about 197 bcf. In 1995, eastern storage fell by 44 bcf, while producing stocks dropped by 15 bcf.

Most traders said they are expecting a larger drawdown in storage in the West to appear as bitterly cold temperatures blanketed western Canada last week. In 1995 during this period, stocks fell only two bcf to 87 percent of capacity.
